preregistration.decision_rule: positive requires lower_95_cb >= sesoi over independent units; a tie is a null; an effect in the wrong direction is a failure; seeds may not be added after the fact

H1_recurrence.premise: a recurrent state transition provides value a stateless model cannot recover, even with matched parameter count and explicit causal history

H2_explicit_history.premise: the core effect is access to historical observations, and a stateless model given a matched history reproduces it

H3_capacity.premise: the core effect is mainly increased representation capacity

H4_state_horizon.premise: persistent state helps only because it carries information over a minimum useful temporal horizon

H5_optimization.premise: recurrent models appear superior because they optimize more easily under the current training authority

H6_core_horizon_interaction.premise: larger cores help only when state persists sufficiently long

H7_architecture_family.premise: the effect is specific to one recurrent implementation rather than to persistent temporal computation generally

H8_bed_specificity.premise: the effect is real on the two valid controlled beds and does not transfer to a third natural stream

capacity_tier_correction.rule: analysis replaces only the same bed, seed and cell; original receipts remain immutable
